newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks languish on weaker Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks languish on weaker Wall Street.

text.p: Singapore stocks languish in early morning trade on Thursday following Wall Street's decline overnight.

"The mood is not 100 percent hands on to invest here. Most investors are concern about Wall Street's trend," said an institutional dealer. "It looks like there is still some downside to come on Wall Street."

At 0215 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index shed 6.11 points to 2,083.70. Turnover was a paltry 23 million with 173 losers against 29 gainers. The UOB-OTC index measuring Malaysian over the counter shares fell 7.64 points to 1,249.39
Most of the stocks on the actives list comprised block deals, dealers said.
Hong Kong's Mandarin Oriental saw the entire 982,000 shares crossed at US$1.29 while Hotel Properties saw 660,000 shares crossed at S$2.48 (US$1.72).
Keppel Telecommunications & Transportation Ltd topped the percentage losers, shedding 16.55 percent or S$0.24 to S$1.21 as it went ex-rights today.
Dealers said bargain-hunting was still seen in selected banks and property stocks.
